# Sāmagāma Sutta (MN 104 (PTS MN ii 243))

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāmagāma Sutta* (MN 104) is set among the Sakyans at Sāmagāma [Gethin 2001]. Following the recent demise of the Jain leader Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta (Mahāvīra) and the subsequent fracturing of his followers into acrimonious dissension, the novice Cunda and the Venerable Ānanda report the situation to the Buddha out of concern that similar disputes might afflict the Saṅgha after his parinibbāna [Gethin 2001; Tan 2004; Peoples 2012]. The Buddha reassures Ānanda by distinguishing between minor disputes regarding monastic livelihood (*ajjhājīva*) or the disciplinary rules (*pātimokkha*) and critical disputes regarding the path and doctrine (*magga* or *bodhipakkhiya-dhammā*), emphasizing communal unity around the core teachings [Gethin 2001; Freedman 1977; Tan 2004; Peoples 2012].

 DharmaNexus also confirms machine alignments with the Chinese parallels in T 85 and MĀ 196, Sanskrit parallels in the *Adhikaraṇavastu*, *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, and *Saṅgītisūtra*, and Tibetan Vinaya parallels in the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* and *Vinayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
